title: Algebraically trivial lines on a semiabelian variety: inversion and ampleness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $H$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A group scheme has addition, identity and inverse $\iota=[-1]$ satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume $H$ is semiabelian: after an algebraic closure $\bar k/k$ there is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r\to H_{\bar k}\to A\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k[t,t^{-1}]$ and $A$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $\bar k$-group scheme. For a finite-type scheme $X$ over a field, geometric algebraic equivalence means the equivalence relation, after extension to an algebraic closure of the ground field, generated by two fibres of an invertible module on $X\times T$, where $T$ is a smooth connected variety over that algebraic closure. A line is geometrically algebraically trivial when it is equivalent to $\mathcal O_X$ in this sense. Let $P$ and $T$ be invertible modules on $H$ [def-sc-invertible-module] with $T$ geometrically algebraically trivial. Then (i) $\iota^*T\simeq T^\vee$, and hence $T\otimes\iota^*T\simeq\mathcal O_H$; and (ii) $P\otimes T$ is ample if and only if $P$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Both assertions are over $k$, including when $k$ is imperfect or the torus is not split.

source.place: IV (theorem of the cube) and XI, field-level Picard calculus needed for symmetrization; compare Moret-Bailly I 5 and II 3.3.3. Original local WANTED. proof.text: Choose a frame of $e^*T$ and apply the multiplicative-frame-torsor theorem. Its multiplication sends a pair of frames over $(x,y)$ to a frame over $x+y$, equivariantly for $(a,b)\mapsto ab$. Locally trivializing the three lines therefore gives an invertible scalar, and hence an isomorphism $p_1^*T\otimes p_2^*T\simeq m^*T$ on $H\times H$. Pull it back along $x\mapsto(x,-x)$. The right side is the constant line with fibre $e^*T$, trivialized by the chosen frame, so $T\otimes\iota^*T\simeq\mathcal O_H$. The perfect rank-one evaluation pairing identifies the second factor with $T^\vee$, proving (i) over $k$ itself. No isomorphism over an algebraic closure is being descended. Iterating the same multiplication gives $[n]^*T\simeq T^{\otimes n}$ for every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Agent argument from the multiplicative torsor; compare Milne I 8.4--8.5.

proof.text: It remains to prove (ii). Ampleness of either supplied line $P$ or $P\otimes T$ is equivalent to ampleness after $k\subset\bar k$, by relative-ampleness fpqc descent for the structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. This field extension is faithfully flat, affine and quasi-compact, with no separability assumption. Over a field relative ampleness is absolute ampleness. Tensor pullback carries $P\otimes T$ to $P_{\bar k}\otimes T_{\bar k}$. We may thus work over $\bar k$, where the semiabelian extension has split torus, and suppress base-change subscripts. Put $Q=P\otimes T$ and $N=P\otimes\iota^*P$. Step 1 gives $Q\otimes\iota^*Q\simeq N$.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, with T=Spec(k), covering Spec(bar k).

proof.text:
Rigidify $Q$ at the identity by choosing a basis of its one-dimensional identity fibre. The cubical-rigidification theorem applies over the normal base $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$. Write $q_j$ for the isomorphism class of $[j]^*Q$, using additive notation for tensor product; $q_0=0$. Pull the displayed alternating cube tensor of the cubical-line definition back along $x\mapsto([j]x,x,-x)$. Its trivialization says $q_{j+1}+q_{j-1}=2q_j+q_1+q_{-1}$. Starting with $q_0=0$ and $q_1=[Q]$, induction gives
$$q_j=j[Q]+\frac{j(j-1)}2([Q]+[\iota^*Q])\quad(j\geq0):$$
if the formula holds for $j$ and $j-1$, the recurrence gives coefficient $j+1$ on $[Q]$ and coefficient $2\binom j2-\binom{j-1}2+1=\binom{j+1}2$ on the parenthesized class. Thus, using step 2,
$$[n]^*Q\simeq Q^{\otimes n}\otimes N^{\otimes n(n-1)/2}.$$
This is an identity of invertible modules, not merely of numerical classes.

source.place: IV, cube calculus; agent induction written from the alternating cube tensor in def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line.

proof.text: Suppose $P$ is ample. Inversion is an isomorphism, hence an affine morphism: the inverse image of an affine open is isomorphic to that open. Affine pullback preserves ampleness, so $\iota^*P$ is ample. The ample-tensor theorem now makes $N=P\otimes\iota^*P$ ample. No properness of $H$ is needed in either cited statement.

source.place: Tag 0892 for affine pullback; properties.tex, tensor products of ample lines.

proof.text: Apply the relative-ample absolute-twist theorem with $f=\operatorname{id}_H$, its relative line $Q$, and its base line $N$. Here $f$ is quasi-compact. To check its relative-line hypothesis, let $V\subset H$ be affine and $x\in V$. The affine finite-set-section theorem with the singleton $\{x\}$ gives a section $s$ of $Q|_V$ nonvanishing at $x$. The affine-cap-section-open theorem says $V_s$ is affine. Since $V$ is quasi-compact, these are exactly the conditions defining ampleness of $Q|_V$. Thus $Q$ is relatively ample for the identity, and the cited twist theorem yields a bound $a_0$ such that $Q\otimes N^{\otimes a}$ is ample for every $a\geq a_0$.

source.place: Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample), f=id; affine-section and nonvanishing inputs as cited.

proof.text:
Choose $a\geq a_0$ with $n=2a+1$ invertible in $\bar k$. Such $a$ are arbitrarily large: in characteristic 2 every odd $n$ works, in odd characteristic $p$ choose $a$ a sufficiently large multiple of $p$, and in characteristic zero there is no restriction. Step 3 gives
$$[n]^*Q\simeq(Q\otimes N^{\otimes a})^{\otimes n},$$
which is ample by step 5 and the positive-tensor-power theorem. The semiabelian multiplication theorem gives that $[n]$ is finite, etale and surjective; its hypotheses hold for our split semiabelian $\bar k$-scheme, viewed as an algebraic space. By the etale definition it is flat and locally of finite presentation, hence finite locally free by its definition. Finite locally free ample reflection therefore shows $Q$ ample. This proves the forward implication for an arbitrary ample $P$. Tensoring each family in an algebraic-equivalence chain with its dual shows that $T^\vee$ is also geometrically algebraically trivial. Apply the forward implication with $Q$ in place of $P$ and $T^\vee$ in place of $T$ to obtain the converse, since $Q\otimes T^\vee\simeq P$. Finally step 2 descends both implications to $k$.

Item: statement unchanged from base; no re-split note applies. I checked all six steps against the cited statements. (1) The torsor's group law is bi-equivariant, which gives m*T≅p1*T⊗p2*T; pulling back along (1,ι) gives ι*T≅T^∨ over k itself. (2) Stacks 0D3C fpqc descent along Spec k̄→Spec k; over an affine base, relative ampleness is absolute ampleness. (3) I recomputed the cube pullback along ([j],1,−1): q_{j+1}+q_{j−1}=2q_j+q_1+q_{−1}. The induction holds for j=0,1,2 and the coefficients (j+1) and 2C(j,2)−C(j−1,2)+1=C(j+1,2) are right. The cube theorem's case (b) hypotheses hold over the normal base Spec k̄. (4) Inversion is affine (Stacks 0892(2)). Only the first sentence of lem-sc-ample-tensor (any scheme over a field) is used. (5) For f=id, Q|_V is ample on each affine V via the singleton section plus affine-cap; this matches Stacks 0892(1). (6) n=2a+1 is prime to p (take a≡0 mod p, any odd n in char 2), so [n]*Q≅(Q⊗N^a)^n. [n] is finite étale surjective, hence finite locally free; reflection gives Q ample. The converse uses T^∨. New node finite-locally-free reflection: true; I read Stacks 0BD2, 0BCY and the proof of 0BD0 (the norm of the given ample line is ample, and Norm(f*L)=L^d). Varying rank is handled by finitely many open-closed pieces. It is strictly more general than lem-trf-finite-surjective-ample-reflection (proper over a Noetherian ring). New node multiplicative torsor: I checked it is true over imperfect k and for nonsplit tori. Λ(T) is trivial over k̄. Sansuc's sequence plus the Picard scheme of B² gives triviality over k_s. The Galois H^1(X^*) part is killed by triviality on both axes. The normalized trivialization is unique, so E is a commutative G_m-extension. Torus test: Ext^1(T0,G_m)≅H^1(k,X^*)≅Pic(T0). It is not a restatement of the item.
